It is possible that discharge currents may attract trout and other fish to the area of the intake-discharge structure. However, this problem, and the potential for disruption of stratification, may be reduced by constructing an underwater weir in the Whitewater River Arm of Lake Jocassee, 1600 ft. downstream of the discharge structure, see Exhibit W, Figure 1.4-1, Amendment 1. The weir will consist of 400,000 to 500,000 cubic yards of rock which will be excavated from underground tunnels. The crest of the weir will extend to within 60 ft. of full good elevation. During warm months, the weir will extend up through the thermocline, thus forming a barrier between the suitable trout habitat in the lake, and the mixed turbulent water near the discharge (see enclosure report by Billy Edge).
